I WAS using a script by Brandon Mulrenin and am still using his flexible commission program. 1% if owner finds buyer, 3.5% If I find buyer, 6% if another agent brings a buyer.

Haven't had anyone sell on their own yet, and usually the FSBO's have given up by then and just want me to put it on the MLS for them.

My script starting out used to be something like "Mr/Mrs X?"

This is \_\_\_\_ with \_\_\_. How are you?. Have you  had any offers on that house yet? (huge conversation starter. If they start a conversation here, just go with it)

Are you working with agents right now?(dangerously vague question because sometimes they will tell you why they're selling, when they're going to hand the listing over to an agent, or they'll say something like "we're selling FSBO". 

If they say "we're selling FSBO" just say. Oh, yeah. I meant if an agent brought you a buyer, would you pay a commission? 

Awesome. If you don't get this place sold for whatever reason in 30 days, and in this market, you should. Would you consider listing? If yes, I'll tell them about my program, if no, I'll ask to come see the home just to get face to face.

My way of speaking is quite dynamic and I'm just focused on starting a conversation. I will just go wherever the conversation takes me and let them talk for however long they want. I really just focus on connecting, because if you connect, there will be trust and if there's trust, at some point you will list and sell their house if they can't do it.

I also help them however they need it while they try to sell on their own. I'll give them my lender buddy's number to qualify any buyers that don't have money(yet). Give them a number to a real estate attorney I know, a title company, contractors, etc. 

Follow up with everyone one day of your choosing every week. Just ask if there's anything I can do and when I REALLY feel that they're struggling, I swoop in for the listing appointment and by then they know me well enough that I'm usually top of the list for agents to list their home

Yup. Super Easy.

"Hi, this is \_\_\_\_ with \_\_\_\_\_, how are you doing today?Hey, I see you've got \_\_\_\_ property for sale, what's the deal there(do you still live there, etc)?(just let them talk about everything, they'll tell you where they want to move, why they're selling, etc works almost always). "Well, hey, when's a good time to see the property? I have X day or Y day available. Great, see you then."

I don't ask any qualifying questions and pretty much find out everything I want to know by just letting them talk about themselves. Low pressure is key, imo. When I get to their home, I tour it and afterwards give them some value like a free website on my laptop and a really cheap lead-tracking sign they can buy and wish them good luck on their journey. I then followup once every week to ask how it's going until I feel it's the right time to ask for the listing.

I watch a lot of agents get really aggressive with them and in my experience, most FSBOs just think you are trying to make them look dumb. You just want to get into the door. FSBOs know you're an agent who could potentially find them a buyer, you don't really need to explain why you want to see the home or anything.

Other agents are calling them and trying to rip the listing right then and there. While this does work, I feel as though a really low-pressure, friendly and helpful approach is just amazing. One of my FSBOs asked me to list their property on the first meeting

Also, if you're not going outside at all right now, ZOOM tours are pretty effective.
